newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Taiwan minister visits Malaysia, seeing "friends".
newsitem.headline: Taiwan minister visits Malaysia, seeing "friends".

text.p: Taiwan Foreign Minister John Chang, visiting Malaysia in defiance of China's attempts to block the island's diplomatic offensive, said on Saturday he was there to meet "a lot of friends".

In the first confirmation of a controversial visit which began on Friday, Chang told a Taiwanese television station that, after his stay in Kuala Lumpur, he planned to see other friends in the region and elsewhere.
"I will meet a lot of friends not only in Southeast Asia but also from other places," he told Taiwan Television Enterprise Ltd. A clip of the short interview was viewed by Reuters.
Taiwan's Foreign Ministry has declined to comment on the visit and Malaysian officials were tight-lipped about Chang's presence.
"At this particular juncture, we are not able to shed any light," a Malaysian Foreign Ministry official told Reuters.

On Friday, in an airport interview in Singapore, Chang had blamed Beijing's communist government for the secrecy cloaking his Malaysia journey, which -- like an equally furtive trip to Indonesia on Wednesday -- was sure to anger China.
"As we don't have diplomatic ties (with Malaysia), I had to keep my departure secret," said Chang, who reportedly was travelling under an alias.
"Due to pressure from the mainland China side, I could not reveal my plans to the media beforehand," he said.
Once in Kuala Lumpur, looking relaxed in a dark suit in the lobby of a leading hotel, he told the television company he wanted people to know of Taiwan's existence.
He declined to confirm or deny that he was meeting officials from the Malaysian Foreign Ministry.
He was expected to leave for home on Sunday morning.
Communist China has considered Taiwan a renegade province not entitled to international recognition since the Nationalists lost the Chinese Civil War in 1949 and took refuge on the island.
China announced on Friday it had admonished Indonesia for letting Chang have what Jakarta took pains to call an unofficial meeting with Foreign Minister Ali Alatas on Wednesday.

Such "holiday diplomacy" by Taiwan leaders boldly defies China's persistent calls for the wealthy but diplomatically isolated island to quit its drive for a United Nations seat and a higher international profile.

"Visiting overseas is very normal," Chang told Taiwan's Chinese Television during his Singapore transit stop on Friday. "To exchange ideas and have contacts with foreign countries -- this is very important."

Chinese President Jiang Zemin said on Friday that Taipei should prove it was sincere in its desire for senior-level talks by ending efforts to raise its international profile and climb out of its isolation.
"If the Taiwan authorities are indeed sincere about holding meetings, they should give up their political plot of creating "two Chinas' or "one-China, one-Taiwan'," Jiang said.
"Two Chinas" and "one-China, one-Taiwan" are euphemisms used by Beijing to describe Taipei's attempts to raise its profile.
